evidence_scope: uncommitted M4 working tree based on source_commit

profiles: deterministic in-memory RF3 Raft plus replication controller
real RF1 segmented WAL close/reopen and committed-prefix replay

commands.result: all M0 through M4 packages passed
all storage, Raft, ISR/HW/ack-gate, model, and subprocess tests passed
all M0 through M4 packages and subprocess tests passed under the race detector

acceptance.RP-06: the M3 isolated-old-leader and ReadIndex regression remains in the full gate; M4 Fetch additionally requires a controller-owned current-term ReadState
acceptance.RP-08: partial current-term progress refreshes last_success_at but not last_caught_up_at; a peer that misses its captured target past the lag window is evicted while a caught-up peer remains
acceptance.RP-09: an operation captured A=[1,2,3], committed by quorum after peer 3 stopped, remained pending after ISR shrank to [1,2], timed out outcome-unknown, and then succeeded through a new A=[1,2] gate at the same log index with no append
acceptance.RP-10: NOOP, two-record DATA, and FENCE committed through internal index 3 produce HW=2; a later uncommitted DATA raises LEO but is excluded from Fetch
acceptance.RP-11: an evicted follower cannot rejoin from an old-term ACK or a below-target ACK; a current-term durable ACK at the catch-up target permits re-entry
acceptance.OP-03: min_isr, pending-operation, byte, history, and fetch-waiter caps reject before append or ReadIndex allocation; retries reacquire capacity and one operation cannot accumulate concurrent gates
acceptance.OP-04: test-only operation identity survives reply timeout inside the live controller, preserves index and offsets, and creates a bounded new gate without automatic ack downgrade

actions: propose DATA through min_isr and captured-A admission
deliver or drop a random queued Raft RPC
retry an existing operation with a new request gate
per_event_assertions: leader remains in its own ISR and ISR stays sorted and bounded by voters
HW equals the DATA end mapped from the applied internal prefix and never exceeds LEO
captured ISR, operation index, and terminal gate result never mutate
every succeeded gate is applied and every captured follower has durable_match_index at or beyond the operation index
pending operation and byte accounting remains exact and within configured caps
model_testing.raft_regression: the independent M3 deterministic model also runs 100 seeds x 1000 events

additional_results: Raft emits a DurableAck only for a current-term AppendResponse tied to the exact tracked RPC; unknown and duplicate responses emit none.
RF1 completes the captured-self gate locally, persists DATA and commit state, reconstructs HW=1 after close/reopen, and serves the record only after a new-term leader barrier and ReadIndex.
ISR is not used for RequestVote eligibility, voter membership, or Raft quorum calculations.
A timed-out request can be outcome-unknown while its quorum-committed DATA is already visible below HW.
Every M0-M3 format, storage, crash-recovery, sparse-index, Raft model, and three-process regression remains in the full gate.
output_location: This scrubbed evidence manifest; no payload bytes, credentials, or large process artifacts are retained.
limitations: M4 exposes an internal controller, not a running broker, HTTP Produce/Fetch handler, client retry loop, or long-poll event loop.
Operation identity and acknowledgement-gate history are memory-resident and bounded; restart-stable producer identity, epoch, sequence, digest, dedup cache, and fencing belong to M5.
The RF3 M4 fault schedule is deterministic and in-memory; real-process RF3 failover/restart coverage is inherited from M3, while M4 adds real-filesystem RF1 HW recovery.
Retention, snapshots, consumer groups, transactions, dynamic membership, authentication, and Kafka wire compatibility do not exist.
next_task: M5: implement durable producer identity, epoch fencing, sequence and digest validation, committed replay, bounded dedup results, public Produce API, and retrying Go client/CLI evidence.
